head.message:
fix(view): keep backend scope out of generated script (#412)

* fix(view): keep backend scope out of generated script

* fix(view): don't report success for a server that never came up

The generated script now throws if its argv contract is not met, and it runs
detached with `stdio: "ignore"` — so that throw goes nowhere. The CLI checked
only that spawn returned a pid, then printed "[ok] Visualizer started", wrote a
PID file for a dead process and opened a browser on a closed port.

`view-server.test.ts` already had `waitForPort` for exactly this reason ("a
server that dies on startup would otherwise surface as a timeout ... invisibly,
because stdio is ignored"). This gives the command the same check.

Reported rather than fatal, and the process is left alone: 8s is a heuristic,
and on a machine slow enough to exceed it, killing the server or failing the
command would be worse than the mis-report. The PID/scope/port files are written
either way, so `ix view status` and `ix view stop` still work.

`view-running-port.test.ts` mocked `createConnection` to always refuse, which
answered the pre-spawn "is this port taken?" check but hangs a post-spawn
readiness probe for its whole budget. The mock now models the transition.

* test(view): cover runtime server arguments

---------

Co-authored-by: KageBinary <ianjakobhock@gmail.com>
